headline_marked: BRTC launches [[women-only 'Pink Bus' service]] for safer transport
headline: BRTC launches women-only 'Pink Bus' service for safer transport
summary: The new service features female drivers and conductors to ensure a comfortable commute for women across five major cities.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has officially launched the 'Pink Bus' service to provide women with a safer and more comfortable public transport option.
The service was inaugurated by Road Transport and Bridges, Railway and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam at the BRTC Tejgaon Bus Depot.
According to the BRTC, the buses will operate on designated routes in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Bogura, and Chattogram starting tomorrow.
A unique feature of the service is that the buses will be operated by female drivers and conductors, further enhancing the sense of security for female passengers.
Beyond transport, there are suggestions to use the pink color of the buses as a platform for breast cancer awareness, as pink is the global symbol for the cause.
Proposed additions include displaying health information and warning signs inside the buses and using pink lights at night to remind women to stay aware of their breast health.
This initiative aims to turn a daily commute into an opportunity for health education, especially leading up to 'Pink October', the global Breast Cancer Awareness Month.
caption:
Safe, comfortable, and driven by women. BRTC's new 'Pink Bus' service is here!

The Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation (BRTC) has officially launched the 'Pink Bus' service to provide women with a safer and more comfortable public transport option.

The service was inaugurated by Road Transport and Bridges, Railway and Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam at the BRTC Tejgaon Bus Depot.

According to the BRTC, the buses will operate on designated routes in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Bogura, and Chattogram starting tomorrow.

A unique feature of the service is that the buses will be operated by female drivers and conductors, further enhancing the sense of security for female passengers.

Beyond transport, there are suggestions to use the pink color of the buses as a platform for breast cancer awareness, as pink is the global symbol for the cause.

Proposed additions include displaying health information and warning signs inside the buses and using pink lights at night to remind women to stay aware of their breast health.

This initiative aims to turn a daily commute into an opportunity for health education, especially leading up to 'Pink October', the global Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

headline_marked: Wedding cancelled: [[Father calls off marriage]] after groom argues over whole goat
headline: Wedding cancelled: Father calls off marriage after groom argues over whole goat
summary: A bride's father in Brahmanbaria refused to marry his daughter to a Japan-based groom after a dispute over the wedding feast menu.
details: In Brahmanbaria's Akhaura Upazila, a wedding was abruptly cancelled after the groom entered into a heated argument with the bride's family over the absence of a whole goat in the special meal.

The incident occurred in Tolatala village of Dharkhar Union on Monday. The groom, Junayed Mia, a resident of Kosba's Niamatpur village and a Japan expatriate, reportedly expressed dissatisfaction with the floral welcome and the food served.

According to the bride's father, Sofikul Islam, the groom objected to the lack of a whole goat in the special food trays provided for him and his close relatives. When the father explained that it hadn't been requested and would be served at a later event, the argument escalated.

The father further claimed that during the dispute, the groom told him to marry his own brother instead. Consequently, the bride's family decided to cancel the wedding and asked the groom's party, including 150 guests, to leave with their gifts and jewelry.

However, Junayed Mia posted on Facebook on Tuesday, claiming a different version of events. He alleged that the bride's family demanded a dower (kabin) ten times higher than the agreed amount after the meal, leading to the dispute.
A local Union Parishad member, Ashik Mia, confirmed the incident, stating that the groom's rude behavior regarding the food led the father to call off the marriage.
The story has since sparked widespread discussion and criticism on social media platforms.
